outputText:
A long, nonsensical string of "LLM-related" keywords (cache, kernel, tensor, logit, batch, etc.) preceded by a "LocalMaxxing cache-bust nonce." This is a common technique used to bypass certain filters or just to create a "noisy" prompt.
"Explain why local inference speed tests should report prompt prefill throughput, decode throughput, and time to first token."
The user wants a technical explanation of three specific metrics in the context of Large Language Model (LLM) inference.

    *   *Prompt Prefill:* The phase where the model processes the input prompt. It's computationally heavy (matrix multiplications) but highly parallelizable.
    *   *Decode:* The phase where the model generates tokens one by one. It's memory-bandwidth bound because it processes one token at a time.
    *   *Time to First Token (TTFT):* The latency from sending the prompt to receiving the first character.
    *   *Throughput:* The amount of data processed per second (tokens/sec).

    *   *Why report Prefill Throughput?*
        *   It measures the efficiency of the "thinking" phase.
